name: Equipment Maintenance & Replacement (Funds 671 and 672)

established.purpose: Internal service funds that bill departments for vehicle maintenance (672) and bank replacement charges to buy vehicles when they age out (671); the ACFR reports them as one fund

legal_basis: Internal service fund; charges set in the budget; Fleet Replacement Fund Short Millions audit (June 2, 2021) recommended an Administrative Regulation requiring documented justification before transfers out

annual.note: Internal service combining statement, ACFR FY2024 p.311-312
Combining Statement of Revenues, Expenses and Changes in Net Position, Internal Service Funds, ACFR p.321

flows.instrument: FY2024 budget / AAO (per Fleet Audit presentation, Feb 27, 2025)
flows.stated_reason: Operating expenses of the maintenance fund paid from the replacement fund
flows.note: Shown in the combined ACFR fund as transfers out $500,000 in FY2024.

flows.instrument: FY2025 budget / AAO (per Fleet Audit presentation, Feb 27, 2025)
flows.stated_reason: Operating expenses of the maintenance fund paid from the replacement fund
flows.note: The audit's recommendation 1.6, an Administrative Regulation requiring written justification before such transfers, was still 'partly implemented' in October 2025.

flows.stated_reason: General Fund and CIP contributions to equipment replacement

flows.instrument: FY2026 AAO Amendment, Consent Item 8, November 18, 2025

obligations.note: Fund 671 balance $7.43M (FY2019) to $19.74M (FY2025); $50.3M spent or encumbered on replacement since FY2019; 46 units a year replaced on average (7.4% of the fleet). The audit found the fund short by millions against a full replacement schedule; no dollar figure for the gap is published
Electric conversion of the Zero Waste fleet: about $9.0M of additional vehicle cost plus $6.5M of chargers (staff estimate)

status.years_in_deficit: Operating surplus both years; the question is whether replacement charges are adequate and whether the balance stays in the fund
open_questions: Which fund the FY2025 $2.0M transfer in beyond the GF and CIP contributions came from (combined fund shows transfers in $3,759,380).
